paragraphs: 看著立德上尉的眼，雷亞感到不適。說好的給他一天的時間考慮，立德上尉雖然看起來還算冷靜，但依然充滿壓迫感。拉比嘗試和立德上尉溝通，卻發現上尉完全不把他放在眼裡。眼看變回蜥蜴人的雷亞不正面做出答覆，立德上尉背後軍營的入口開始出現更多的士兵，站在他身後。一開始，他們只是壓迫感強大的士兵們，隨著他們開始逼近，冒險者們發現士兵們口中充滿各種惡言與辱罵，絲毫不把他們放在眼裡，而立德上尉也沒有對此有任何的制止或意見。拉比快要按捺不住，把臉抵在立德上尉臉前，卻感到肚子一陣陣痛。才剛從醫院離開不久的他，被立德上尉用腳踩在地上，還吐了口口水唸到「藍色的狗」。
眼看局面僵持不下，老樹盟的士兵們看來也不是能溝通的類型，毛毛試圖說服立德上尉，讓雷亞可以了解一下其他勢力現在的狀況再給予答覆。立德上尉給了隔天日落的最終寬限，便領著老樹盟的士兵們回到軍營內了。他自己則在冒險者們離開時，站在軍營入口默默看著。雷亞雖然還不確定未來應該倒向哪個勢力，但他很清楚老樹盟不在他的考慮範圍內了。
拉比領著大家往新書院的聚集處，也就是他們之前見皮尼歐教授的學校辦公室走。雖然他對新上位的「秘書長」瓦羅恩沒什麼好感，但他畢竟是新書院出生的人，過去皮尼歐教授的理想也與冒險者們最接近，還是值得談一談，至少了解一下狀況也好。

接近辦公室時，拉比就感受到完全不一樣的氛圍了。辦公室外站了四名學生衛兵，比起過去皮尼歐教授時期的衛兵，他們不僅沒有正規的配備，眼神還充滿了戾氣。看著拉比走道門前，一名衛兵擋住了他，要他報上名來。拉比說了自己的名字與來意，衛兵卻還是對他不太信任。拉比掏出了老舊的黨徽，衛兵們看起來充滿不屑，也還是讓他們進辦公室內了。辦公室內今非昔比，數不盡的年輕學生們把辦公室當成交誼廳大聲嚷嚷，毫無秩序，而裡面那間關起門來的會議室，似乎就是瓦羅恩秘書長所在的地方。冒險者們聽從指示，等等進入秘書長的辦公室時必須大聲地喊「秘書長好！」來表示對秘書長的敬意。然後一名學生衛兵便將會議室的門打開。
辦公室內，瓦羅恩秘書長正低頭抄寫著，一名學生衛兵在門邊怒瞪著冒險者們，質疑他們怎麼沒有向秘書長問好。雖然覺得很誇張怪異，但拉比還是帶頭喊了聲「秘書長好！」除了羅羅外，其他冒險者們也配合打了招呼。然而，羅羅的行為被學生衛兵抓到並刁難，最終拉比只好假裝羅羅的聲音喊了聲「秘書長好！」，學生衛兵才讓他們入內。

關上門，冒險者們向瓦羅恩秘書長請教，但秘書長完全沒有抬頭想和他們認真溝通的意思。冒險者們說明了雷亞的狀況，也想知道現在新書院的立場。瓦羅恩秘書長的回覆，不僅對新書院現在的路線與理念避而不談，甚至讓冒險者們懷疑他的上位是不是用了不正當的手段，或者可能有其他勢力介入也說不定。對於瓦羅恩秘書長，雷亞也不太敢恭維。瓦羅恩秘書長反覆用「你們這麼聰明，當然知道應該要支持新書院對吧？」這種空泛卻又高傲的態度，讓冒險者們感到不太舒適。
有人敲了敲會議室關上的門。一名學生押著另一名學生走了進來。和秘書長打了聲招呼後，學生表示他押著的這名學生是間諜，因為他質疑新書院的理念。瓦羅恩秘書長沒有多想，說了聲「如果是間諜，那就把他趕走吧。」學生便被帶離會議室。冒險者在關上門的會議室內，都能聽見那名學生被趕出辦公室外並被欺壓的哀嚎聲。不久後，冒險者便告辭了。

冒險者們感到辦公室外，看著四名門口的學生衛兵正在欺負被趕出辦公室的「間諜」，他的腿似乎已經被打瘸了。拉比出手制止，差點被學生衛兵攻擊，最後衛兵覺得無趣，便回到崗位去了。拉比扛起這名學生，向他詢問到底發生什麼事了？自我介紹名為桓托的學生表示他只是試圖開啟對話，和其他學生討論新書院和新曙光的理念到底是什麼，就被質疑他反動。在他心中，這樣的新書院，已經不是過去皮尼歐教授時期的新書院了，離開也罷。經過桓托的同意後，冒險者們便帶著他回到旅店去。他們計畫讓桓托換掉身上藍色的裝束，穿上羅羅借他的衣服後，一起去市民連線那裡看看。
回到旅店，胡里歐在一樓忙到不行，冒險者們便不打擾他，直接上二樓去了。然而，二樓一片慘狀，冒險者們與羅羅的房間門口都躺滿了喝醉的酒客，地板也骯髒不堪，旁邊的包廂內也充滿了各種態度不佳的食客與酒客。羅羅試圖把一名酒客挪開，讓他能走入房間內，酒客卻抓住了他的腳，讓他感到噁心不堪。在雷亞與拉比的幫忙下，他們終於把兩個門口的酒客搬走，讓羅羅可以進房內拿衣服，其他人則可先到大家的通鋪休息。
通鋪門打開，一片漆黑，只有一個微弱的小光源。照明了房間後，冒險者們看到那個光源來自瑪莉貝爾的手上。瑪莉貝爾表示他從他們撿到的發聲器拆解後做出了這個會發光的裝置。冒險者們對於瑪莉貝爾的能力感到驚奇，但也對他還沒有恢復理智的這回事感到擔心。
羅羅回到大家房內後，將衣服遞給桓托。冒險者們評估現在外面太混亂，要出發去找市民連線不是太好的主意。在得到桓托同意後，他們讓桓托也在房內過夜，大家隔天早上再一起去找市民連線。冒險者們都累壞了，決定提早休息，但也認同這樣的夜晚，一定需要輪班守夜。
雷亞率先守夜。大家很快地入睡了，連瑪莉貝爾也睡著了。雷亞看看窗外，街道還有些紛擾。他聽見了微小的聲音，是夢話。環顧四周，雷亞發現是瑪莉貝爾。他呢喃著「爸爸、媽媽」。心疼的雷亞環抱著瑪莉貝爾，伴著他。瑪莉貝爾的淚水也沾上了雷亞的衣服。
時間差不多，雷亞喚了拉比起來守夜，他也不移動身體，讓瑪莉貝爾可以安穩地依偎在他懷中。拉比起身，看見雷亞入眠後，走到了房外。他看見胡里歐正在將二樓喝醉的酒客們一一搬下樓。他則踏出酒館外，找了街燈旁開始寫信。一段時間後，拉比把信綁在他的梟腳上，讓梟飛往遠方，然後他就回房內去了。

輪到鑰守夜時，他想起在克萊芬的這幾天。對他來說，這裡的政治紛亂是他從未想像過的，雖然也新鮮，但更多的是不解。他想起他的母親，便在腦中傳了個消息，想從他母親那裡了解，為何這些人會在有相同敵人的前提下互相算計與傷害？「每個人都有自己的目標，在達成前，大家會以自己的利益優先。」母親回覆他。不久後，鑰聽到房內有挪動身軀的聲音。轉頭一看，瑪莉貝爾默默地移動到他身旁，輕輕地把頭靠在他身上。他的眼睛是睜開的。「我想念阿龍。」瑪莉貝爾輕聲說道。「我也是。」鑰也說道。兩人輕聲討論後，決定傳訊息給阿龍，因為不想讓阿龍擔心，瑪莉貝爾希望告訴阿龍大家都還好，鑰也這樣把訊息傳給了阿龍。不久後，他便得到了阿龍的答覆「知道大家都過得很好，實在是太好了。掰掰」。
瑪莉貝爾睡著了。因為沒有先安排好下一班由誰守夜，鑰想著羅羅應該不用睡覺，便找了團紙，丟向羅羅，示意輪到他守夜。這對平常都自己睡一間的羅羅有點不習慣，但他也不想冒險回到自己的房門口。要是門口還有噁心的醉漢，那就讓他更抓狂了。

羅羅靠在牆邊思忖。他毫無睡意，但天也還沒亮，夥伴們肯定也還沒睡飽。對於不習慣在他人面前顯露自己情緒的他來說，這段時間的這一切事件轟炸，讓他有點喘不過氣，情緒也還沒有理乾淨。他陷入自己的沉思，卻突然聽見一聲熟悉的聲音在他腦中浮現「你怎麼啦？」那是來自宗主的聲音，既令人感到恐懼與厭惡，那傢伙卻又給予他存在的意義。「不要再抓了。」當他聽見這句話時，才突然意識到自己的手正猛地抓著自己的臉。他嚇到，停了下來，但腦中冒出了更多不同聲音的同一句話「不要再抓了。」但羅羅已經沒有再抓了。他情緒緊繃，有點喘不過氣，開始恐慌，然後用力捶了牆壁一拳。
這一拳驚醒了拉比。拉比起身走到羅羅身邊，詢問他是否還好。羅羅故作鎮定裝沒事，也沒有讓拉比看見他的臉，但拉比還是坐了下來，想和羅羅聊聊。面對這個，羅羅更不知所措。他不太習慣和人聊內心的想法。拉比試著引導羅羅。「對你來說，神是什麼意義？」羅羅問道。在他心中，宗主有如神一般的存在，但又有太多無法理解或與他想法衝突的地方。「人的生命，是可以被死而復生的嗎？」

談話後，拉比要羅羅先去休息。醒來後，他已難以再入睡。拉比走了下樓，看見忙了一整晚的胡里歐趴在櫃檯睡著了。他也在櫃檯旁嘗試像胡里歐一樣趴著睡，但不久後，他發現不好睡，便起身離開了。酒館大門的門縫，拉比撿到了一份當天的日報。頭版是聳動的大字「混血之子雷亞現身克萊芬」，撰稿人是克萊芬之聲的資深記者瑞森。拉比翻了翻報紙，發現相較於這篇外，報紙內關於皮尼歐教授之死以及新曙光，都只有非常小篇幅的文章，甚至關於市長改選，都還沒有新消息。拉比把報紙放在一張桌子上。這時，他看見他的梟飛回來了。在他碰到梟的那一刻，他的腦中浮現了一個聲音說著「需要幫忙的時候我會出現」。那是久違的柳俠馬許的聲音。接著，拉比便走回二樓去了。
不久後，天亮了。冒險者們起床前，拉比回到了一樓，眼看幾乎沒睡的胡里歐已經起身開始為一大早來到酒館的客人準備早餐，拉比接下了這份工，讓胡里歐可以先休息。拉比在吧台掛了張牌子，寫著「今日只供應主廚早餐」，便踏入廚房做早餐了。一名客人對於拿到的餐點和他點的不一樣十分不滿，但拉比表示不吃就什麼都沒有，讓客人也只能摸摸鼻子接受了。

冒險者們一一下樓，向拉比點了主廚早餐，便坐了下來。不久後，他們發現酒館外擠滿了人，口中嚷者「混血之子」、「雷亞」等。他們紛紛擠入店內，有的問雷亞他的身份，有的問他對於與老樹盟合作有什麼想法，也有新書院的支持者對雷亞十分不滿。鑰和瑪莉貝爾決定把早餐拿到樓上去，雷亞也嘗試往樓上跑，人們追著他跑上了樓梯。趁著空檔，雷亞變身成一隻蟑螂，讓人們撲了空。這時，跑得比較快的瑪莉貝爾已經來到包廂門口，但鑰還卡在樓梯上，周圍都是暴民。瑪莉貝爾深吸一口氣，掏出他的日記本，朝著樓梯一比，口中念念有詞。瞬間，樓梯上的人們，包含鑰在內，都陷入了睡眠。
雷亞從樓梯縫隙跳到拉比身上，擺動他的觸鬚。拉比意識到這是雷亞的化身，便嘗試與他溝通。對於老樹盟的不守信用，先讓媒體告知大眾雷亞「混血之子」的身份，甚至預設他會為老樹盟站台一事，雷亞感到訝異。拉比認為克萊芬現在的狀況已經待不了了，但在離開克萊芬前，他有個地方想帶雷亞去。
「城鎮外有個樹林間的小教堂，我想帶你們去那裡，把一些事情說清楚。」他說道。

Leah felt uneasy as she looked into Captain Reid's eyes. He had promised to give her a day to consider his offer, and although he still appeared calm, there was an oppressive force behind him. Ravi tried to speak with Captain Reid, but quickly realized that the captain did not regard him at all. When Leah, back in her lizardfolk form, refused to answer him directly, more soldiers began appearing at the entrance to the military camp behind Captain Reid, taking up positions behind him. At first, they were simply imposing soldiers. But as they drew closer, the adventurers heard the stream of insults and abuse coming from their mouths. They treated the adventurers as if they were beneath notice, and Captain Reid made no attempt to stop them or object. Ravi was about to lose his temper and pressed his face close to Captain Reid's, only to feel a sharp pain in his stomach. Not long after leaving the clinic, he was kicked to the ground by Captain Reid, who spat on him and muttered, "Blue dog."

With the standoff showing no sign of ending, and the Old Tree League soldiers clearly unwilling to talk, Fur tried to persuade Captain Reid to let Leah learn about the other factions' current situations before giving him an answer. Captain Reid granted her a final extension until sunset the next day, then led the Old Tree League soldiers back into the camp. He himself remained at the entrance, silently watching the adventurers as they left. Leah still did not know which faction she should support, but she knew for certain that the Old Tree League was no longer under consideration.

Ravi led everyone toward the New Academy's gathering place: the school office where they had met Professor Peneo before. He had little fondness for Varoen, the new secretary-general, but she had been raised within the New Academy, and Professor Peneo's ideals had once aligned most closely with those of the adventurers. It was still worth talking to her, if only to understand the situation.

As they neared the office, Ravi immediately sensed that the atmosphere had changed. Four student guards stood outside. Compared with the guards from Professor Peneo's time, they had neither proper equipment nor disciplined expressions; their eyes were filled with hostility. When Ravi approached the door, one of them stopped him and demanded his name. Ravi gave his name and explained why they had come, but the guard still regarded him with suspicion. Ravi took out the old party badge. The guards looked at it with contempt, but they let the group into the office anyway. Inside, everything had changed. Countless young students had turned the office into a noisy common room, shouting without any sense of order, while the closed meeting room deeper inside appeared to be where Secretary-General Varoen was staying. The adventurers were told that when they entered the secretary-general's office, they had to shout "Good day, Secretary-General!" to show their respect. A student guard then opened the meeting-room door.

Inside, Secretary-General Varoen was bent over her writing, while a student guard at the door glared angrily at the adventurers and demanded to know why they had not greeted the secretary-general. Though the whole thing felt absurd and bizarre, Ravi took the lead and called out, "Good day, Secretary-General!" Everyone except Roel played along and returned the greeting. The guard caught Roel's silence and began giving him trouble, so Ravi finally imitated Roel's voice and shouted, "Good day, Secretary-General!" Only then did the guard let them enter.

Once the door was closed, the adventurers asked Secretary-General Varoen for guidance, but she did not even look up and showed no interest in speaking with them seriously. They explained Leah's situation and asked about the New Academy's current position. Varoen's answer avoided discussing both the academy's present course and its ideals, leaving the adventurers to wonder whether she had taken power through improper means, or whether another faction had intervened. Leah was no more impressed by Varoen. The secretary-general repeatedly adopted a vague yet arrogant tone, saying things like, "You are all so clever. Surely you know that you should support the New Academy, don't you?" Her manner made the adventurers deeply uncomfortable.

Someone knocked on the meeting-room door. A student entered, escorting another student. After greeting the secretary-general, he said that the student he had brought in was a spy because he had questioned the New Academy's ideals. Varoen gave the matter no thought and simply said, "If he is a spy, then throw him out." The student was dragged out of the meeting room. Even with the door closed, the adventurers could hear his cries as he was driven from the office and abused outside. Not long afterward, they said their farewells.

When the adventurers stepped outside the office, they saw the four student guards at the door bullying the "spy" they had thrown out. His leg appeared to have been badly injured. Ravi intervened and nearly came under attack from the guards, but they eventually lost interest and returned to their posts. Ravi carried the student on his back and asked what had happened. The student introduced himself as Juanto and explained that he had merely tried to start a discussion with the other students about what the New Academy and New Dawn were supposed to mean. He had been accused of being a reactionary for doing so. In his eyes, this New Academy was no longer the New Academy of Professor Peneo's time, and leaving it behind was no great loss. With Juanto's consent, the adventurers took him back to the tavern. They planned to have Juanto change out of his blue clothes, put on clothes Roel had lent him, and then go together to see the Citizen's Connection.

Back at the tavern, Julio was far too busy on the first floor for the adventurers to bother him, so they went straight upstairs. The second floor was a disaster. Drunken patrons were sprawled across the doors to both the adventurers' room and Roel's room, the floor was filthy, and the booth beside them was packed with diners and drinkers in foul moods. Roel tried to move one of the patrons so he could enter his room, but the drunk grabbed his leg, leaving him disgusted. With Leah and Ravi's help, they finally moved the two drunks away from the doors so Roel could get inside and retrieve some clothes, while the others went ahead to rest in the shared room.

When the door to the shared room opened, they found it completely dark, except for a faint little light. Once the room was illuminated, the adventurers saw that the light was coming from Maribel's hands. She explained that she had taken apart the speaking device they had found and built this glowing device from it. The adventurers were amazed by Maribel's abilities, but they were also worried that she still had not recovered her senses.

When Roel returned to the shared room, he handed the clothes to Juanto. The adventurers decided that the streets outside were too chaotic, making it unwise to set out for the Citizen's Connection. With Juanto's agreement, they let him spend the night in the room with them and planned to visit the Citizen's Connection together the next morning. Everyone was exhausted and decided to turn in early, but they also agreed that a night like this required taking shifts on watch.

Leah took the first watch. Everyone soon fell asleep, including Maribel. Leah looked out the window at the still-disturbed streets and heard a tiny sound. It was someone talking in their sleep. Looking around, Leah realized it was Maribel. She was murmuring, "Dad... Mom..." Feeling sorry for her, Leah wrapped her arms around Maribel and stayed with her. Maribel's tears dampened Leah's clothes.

When the time came, Leah woke Ravi to take the next watch. She did not move, allowing Maribel to continue resting safely in her arms. Ravi got up, and after seeing Leah fall asleep, he went outside the room. He saw Julio carrying the drunken patrons from the second floor downstairs one by one. Ravi stepped outside the tavern, found a spot beside a streetlamp, and began writing a letter. After some time, he tied the letter to his owl's leg and sent it flying into the distance, then returned to the room.

When it was Kaname's turn to keep watch, she thought about the past few days in Clyphen. The political turmoil here was something she had never imagined. It was fascinating in its own way, but mostly incomprehensible. She thought of her mother and sent a message through her mind, asking why people who shared a common enemy would still scheme against and hurt one another. "Everyone has their own goals. Until those goals are achieved, everyone puts their own interests first," her mother replied. Before long, Kaname heard someone shifting in the room. When she turned, she saw Maribel quietly move to her side and gently rest her head against her. Her eyes were open. "I miss Al-lon," Maribel whispered. "Me too," Kaname replied. After a quiet discussion, they decided to send a message to Al-lon. Maribel wanted to tell him that everyone was safe so he would not worry, and Kaname sent the message for her. Before long, they received Al-lon's reply: "It's wonderful to know that everyone is doing well. Bye-bye."

Maribel fell asleep. Since they had not arranged who would take the next watch, Kaname figured that Roel probably did not need to sleep and threw a ball of paper at him to signal that it was his turn. Roel, who normally slept alone in his own room, found this unfamiliar, but he had no desire to risk returning to his doorway. If disgusting drunks were still lying there, it would drive him even crazier.

Roel leaned against the wall and thought. He was not sleepy at all, but dawn had not yet come, and his companions surely had not slept enough. He was not used to showing his emotions in front of other people, and the barrage of events over the past few days had left him struggling to breathe, with his feelings still in disarray. Lost in thought, he suddenly heard a familiar voice in his mind: "What's wrong?" It was the voice of the Sovereign. The voice frightened and disgusted him, yet that being had also given him a sense of purpose. "Stop scratching." Only when he heard those words did he realize that his hand was clawing violently at his own face. Startled, he stopped, but more voices filled his mind, all repeating the same words: "Stop scratching." Roel was no longer scratching, but his emotions tightened around him. He began to panic and punched the wall with all his strength.

The punch woke Ravi. Ravi got up and went to Roel, asking if he was all right. Roel pretended to be calm and hid his face from Ravi, but Ravi still sat down and tried to talk with him. This left Roel even more at a loss; he was not used to discussing his thoughts with other people. Ravi tried to guide the conversation. "What does a god mean to you?" Roel asked. To him, the Sovereign was like a god, yet there were too many things about him that Roel could not understand or that conflicted with his own thoughts. "Can a person's life be brought back after death?"

After their conversation, Ravi told Roel to get some rest. Once he woke, he found it difficult to fall asleep again. Ravi went downstairs and saw Julio, who had worked through the entire night, asleep with his head on the counter. Ravi tried to sleep beside the counter as Julio had, but soon found it uncomfortable and got back up. Through a gap beneath the tavern's front door, Ravi found that day's newspaper. The front page carried a sensational headline in huge letters: "The Mixed Child Leah Appears in Clyphen." The article was written by Ruisen, a senior reporter for Voice of Clyphen. Ravi flipped through the paper and found that, compared with this story, the articles about Professor Peneo's death and New Dawn were extremely brief. There was not even any new information about the mayoral election. Ravi left the newspaper on a table. At that moment, he saw his owl fly back. The moment he touched it, a voice appeared in his mind: "I will appear when you need help." It was the long-missed voice of Marsh the Willow. Ravi then returned upstairs.

Before long, dawn arrived. Before the adventurers woke, Ravi returned to the first floor and saw that Julio, who had barely slept, was already preparing breakfast for the early customers. Ravi took over the work so Julio could rest. He hung a sign over the counter reading "Today's only offering: the chef's breakfast," then entered the kitchen to cook. One customer complained that the food he received was not what he had ordered, but Ravi told him that if he would not eat it, he would get nothing at all. The customer could only grumble and accept it.

The adventurers came downstairs one by one, ordered the chef's breakfast from Ravi, and sat down. Before long, they realized that the street outside was packed with people shouting things like "mixed child" and "Leah." They surged into the tavern. Some asked Leah about her identity, some asked what she thought about cooperating with the Old Tree League, and some New Academy supporters were openly hostile toward her. Kaname and Maribel decided to take their breakfasts upstairs. Leah also tried to run upstairs, but the crowd chased her up the stairs. At the last moment, Leah transformed into a cockroach and let the crowd rush past. Maribel, who had run faster, had already reached the booth door, but Kaname was still trapped on the staircase among the mob. Maribel took a deep breath, pulled out her journal, pointed it toward the stairs, and began chanting. In an instant, everyone on the staircase, including Kaname, fell asleep.

Leah jumped through a gap in the staircase onto Ravi's body and waved her antennae. Ravi realized that this was Leah in transformed form and tried to communicate with her. Leah was shocked that the Old Tree League had broken its promise: it had allowed the media to announce her identity as a "mixed child" and had even assumed that she would publicly support the league. Ravi believed Clyphen was no longer safe to remain in, but before leaving, he had one place he wanted to take Leah.
"There is a small chapel in the woods outside town. I want to take you there and clear a few things up," he said.
